claim: Adding prompt-based uncertainty estimation components (action confidence, request uncertainty) to an LLM agent reduces task success rate, with the degradation concentrated on demanding tasks and absent on structured tasks, and the effect is attributable to the enlarged prompt rather than architectural changes.
falsifier: On a held-out LLM agent and benchmark, compare task success rate across conditions with increasing uncertainty instrumentation (e.g., baseline, baseline+confidence, baseline+confidence+request uncertainty) while controlling for prompt length and architecture.

conditions: Averaged across five LLM backbones and five benchmarks (WebShop, ALFWorld, REAL, and clarification-augmented variants)
The drop from UAM to the proposed method (0.8 percentage points) is attributable to the enlarged prompt (request-uncertainty signal and explanation) rather than architectural changes
Degradation concentrated on demanding benchmarks (REAL: 32.1%→19.2%; WebShop: 31.9%→26.1%) and absent on structured ALFWorld (57.5%→58.9%)
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported LLM backbones (GPT-5.1, DeepSeek-v3.2-exp, GLM-4.7, Qwen3.5-35B, GPT-OSS-120B), benchmarks, and prompt-based uncertainty methods (ReAct+UE, UAM, proposed decomposition); transfer to other models, tasks, or uncertainty paradigms is unestablished.

title: Addition of uncertainty estimation–Task success rate mechanism
